title: Consolidate routing drain detection and harden fallback resilience after multi-region misroutings
creator: Priya Singh
description: Postmortem and follow-ups for a Feb 12th incident where automated region drains + routing cache TTL mismatch caused large-scale misroutes and cascading fallback to underprovisioned model variants. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and long-term remediation work we completed/triaged.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-12 03:14 UTC, customers in EU-West began seeing elevated latencies and 5xx errors. The control plane initiated an automated drain for a GPU cluster due to underlying hardware ECC warnings. A combination of stale routing cache entries and a mis-ordered drain handshake caused large swaths of traffic to be redirected to a low-cost fallback variant (quantized-8) which exceeded its capacity and triggered cascading fallbacks to smaller variants and rate-limit enforcement. The outage lasted ~42 minutes for impacted tenants and caused reduced throughput and higher tail latency for a subset of PLG customers.
timeline:
2026-02-12 03:12 UTC: Hardware ECC alert on eu-west-a pool.
2026-02-12 03:13 UTC: Control plane issues drain: drain-job(v=4392) created and broadcast.
2026-02-12 03:14 UTC: Edge routing cache still had routes to drained nodes (TTL 300s).
2026-02-12 03:15 UTC: Smart router receives partial drain ack; due to race, routing policy fallback mapping prefers quantized-8 variant (capacity hint low) for some routes.
2026-02-12 03:18 UTC: Quantized-8 variant saturates; autoscaler does not trigger immediately because variant is marked non-scalable.
2026-02-12 03:20 UTC: Router cascades to even smaller variant and applies emergency rate limits. Error rates spike; customers report 5xx and degraded responses.
2026-02-12 03:54 UTC: Hotfix rolled: router logic patched to consult drain authoritative list and drain-proof routing table; traffic shifted to healthy eu-west-b region and rollback of rate limits.
2026-02-12 04:00 UTC: All routes stabilized; full traffic regeneration complete by 04:15 UTC. Post-incident monitoring continued for 24h.
root_cause: Three contributing issues combined: (1) routing cache TTL (300s) allowed stale bindings to persist after control plane drain announcements; (2) drain workflow handshake was not atomic—partial ack states led the router to mis-evaluate node health; (3) fallback variant mapping included a 'non-scalable' flag for quantized-8 which prevented autoscale and made that variant a single point of saturation. A recent config change to reduce cache churn increased TTL but this was not coordinated with drain semantics.
impact: ~1,200 active customers temporarily experienced increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx; platform-wide token throughput reduced by ~18% for ~42 minutes. No customer data loss. Several enterprise tenants hit error budgets and filed incident support tickets.
mitigation: Immediate steps taken during incident: (1) applied hotfix to routing service to prefer authoritative drain list over cached entries; (2) temporarily removed 'non-scalable' tag from quantized-8 variant to enable autoscaling; (3) increased emergency capacity in eu-west-b and diverted traffic; (4) rolled back recent TTL increase for routing cache; (5) reopened affected rate limit windows and lifted emergency throttles.
remediation: Completed and planned remediation items: short-term (done): change routing decision order to check drain authoritative set, revert cache TTL change, enable autoscale on fallback variants, and add immediate alerting for fallback saturation. Medium-term (in progress): implement atomic drain handshake, add read-through cache invalidation on drain events, and add simulation tests for drain+cache interactions. Long-term (backlog): policy engine rewrite to provide capacity-aware fallback selection and canary deployments for fallback variant config changes.
action_items: ENG-8632: Implement atomic drain handshake protocol and gossip propagation (estimate 8)
ENG-8633: Add read-through invalidation hook to routing cache when drain job is accepted (estimate 5)
ENG-8634: Add autoscale opt-in for all fallback variants and default min-instances to 2 (estimate 3)
ENG-8635: Create e2e chaos test for region drain + routing cache TTL interactions (estimate 5)
DOC-472: Update runbook: 'region-drain' section with new verification steps and rollback commands (owner: SRE)
OBS-189: Dashboard tile: 'fallback saturation' with per-variant queue depth and autoscale events (owner: Observability)
PM-501: Policy review to avoid non-scalable fallback as first-choice (owner: Product)
On-call debrief session scheduled: 2026-02-16 16:00 UTC (owner: Diego Martinez)
postmortem_notes: Key lesson: cross-system configuration changes (cache TTL vs drain semantics) require coordinated rollout and test coverage. We underestimated the risk of tagging fallback variants as non-scalable — cost optimization cannot come at availability expense. The immediate fix prioritized deterministic routing behavior (authoritative drain list) and restoring autoscaling resiliency for fallbacks. Follow-ups will harden both the control-plane protocol and the policy engine.
follow_up_status: Several follow-ups already created and assigned (ENG-8632..ENG-8635). SRE completed the runbook update and Observability has a dashboard PR in review. Expected closure of all remediation work by runtime-1.20 quarterly patch.
notes_for_reviews: Requesting reviews from: @Liam O'Connor (Routing), @Ava Patel (SRE), @Maya Rodriguez (Product). Pay special attention to the proposed atomic handshake implementation and the autoscale default for fallback variants. Ensure e2e chaos test covers multi-region and partial-network partitions.
customer_communication: An incident summary was sent to impacted customers on 2026-02-13 and follow-up notes with mitigations were shared on 2026-02-17. Account teams have been given a timeline for remediation and SLA credit offers where appropriate.
